notes: The last note on the slabbed stone ground said that about half of the remaining shimmer was no longer the grooves, but the joins where one kind of stone meets another. That is this note.

A join had no width at all. Every point on the ground picked one stone and took its colour whole, so a pixel sitting on a contact did not shade across it — it belonged entirely to one side, and the smallest camera movement could hand it to the other. Far enough away that a join is thinner than a pixel, walking past made those contacts snap between dark basalt and pale stone.

Now a pixel that straddles a join is given both stones in the proportion it actually covers. Near to, nothing changes at all: a contact you can see is still drawn at full contrast, hard-edged, with each stone its own named colour. The averaging only exists below the size of a pixel, which is precisely where there was never enough room to draw an edge in the first place.
Measured at middle distance, the joins now account for about a fifth of the flicker they did. The cave mouth gets the same treatment, so the ground does not change character where the two meet.
Still to come: the grooves themselves remain most of what moves out there, and that is the harder half — the close-up seam read is judged on them.
The slabbed ground is still a preview: set WAR_GROUND_PLATES=1 before launch to see it.
title: Stone joins stop snapping when you walk past them
